items.title: The Evidence We Do Not Collect
items.topic: how missing data can shape public decisions even when the available statistics are accurate
items.benefit: consistent administrative records allow institutions to track outcomes over time and identify patterns across large populations
items.challenge: people who avoid services, cannot access them, or experience outcomes that are difficult to record may disappear from the evidence used to design policy
items.lesson: decision makers should ask not only whether collected data are accurate but also whose experiences the collection process systematically fails to capture
items.topicJa: 利用できる統計が正確でも収集されないデータが公共の判断を左右する問題
items.benefitJa: 一貫した行政記録は長期的な成果を追跡し大規模な集団の傾向を把握できること
items.challengeJa: サービスを利用しない人や利用できない人、記録しにくい経験を持つ人が政策設計の証拠から消える可能性があること
items.lessonJa: 収集データの正確さだけでなく収集過程が誰の経験を継続的に捉え損ねているかも問う必要がある

items.title: Why a Successful Pilot May Fail at Scale
items.topic: the gap between a small program that works under close supervision and a large system expected to work across varied settings
items.benefit: pilot programs allow new ideas to be tested with limited risk and can reveal practical improvements before wider adoption
items.challenge: early success may depend on unusually motivated staff, extra funding, careful selection, or local conditions that cannot be reproduced everywhere
items.lesson: scaling requires testing which parts of success are essential, which are context dependent, and what capacity must exist before expansion
items.topicJa: 厳密に管理された小規模実験の成功が多様な現場への大規模展開では再現しない場合
items.benefitJa: 試験事業は限定的なリスクで新しい案を試し拡大前に実務上の改善点を見つけられること
items.challengeJa: 初期成功が特に意欲的な人材、追加予算、対象選抜、地域条件など再現しにくい要因に依存する可能性があること
items.lessonJa: 拡大時には成功の必須要素と地域依存要素を分け必要な実施能力を確認する必要がある

items.title: The Fairness of Unequal Support
items.topic: why equal treatment and equitable treatment can lead to different policy choices when people face different barriers
items.benefit: uniform rules are easy to explain, can reduce arbitrary decisions, and give people a clear expectation of what support is available
items.challenge: identical resources may produce unequal opportunities when some people face disability, language, distance, poverty, or other barriers that require additional support
items.lesson: fairness debates should identify whether the goal is equal inputs, equal access, or more equal outcomes because each standard implies different tradeoffs
items.topicJa: 人々が異なる障壁を抱えると同一の扱いと公平な扱いが異なる政策判断につながる理由
items.benefitJa: 一律の規則は説明しやすく恣意的判断を減らし利用可能な支援を明確にできること
items.challengeJa: 障害、言語、距離、貧困などの障壁がある場合同じ資源だけでは機会が平等にならないこと
items.lessonJa: 公平性を論じる際は投入の平等、アクセスの平等、結果の平等のどれを目指すか明確にする必要がある

items.title: When Prevention Looks Inefficient
items.topic: why successful prevention programs can appear unnecessary precisely because the harms they prevent do not occur
items.benefit: preventive measures can reduce future illness, accidents, infrastructure failures, and emergency costs before visible damage develops
items.challenge: when prevention succeeds, observers see the cost of the program but not the avoided event, making benefits difficult to prove and politically easy to discount
items.lesson: evaluating prevention requires credible counterfactual evidence and long time horizons rather than judging value only by events that are directly observed
items.topicJa: 予防策が成功すると防いだ被害が見えないため非効率に見える問題
items.benefitJa: 予防策は病気、事故、設備故障、緊急費用などを被害が現れる前に減らせること
items.challengeJa: 成功時には事業費だけが見え回避された出来事は観察できないため効果を証明しにくく軽視されやすいこと
items.lessonJa: 予防の評価には直接観察された出来事だけでなく信頼できる反実仮想と長期的な視点が必要
